title: WPMS/2350/2015 of M/s Satyam Shivam Sundaram Stone Crusher Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2350 of 2015
M/s Satyam Shivam Sundaram Stone Crusher .Ö.Petitioner
 Vs
State of Uttaakhand & others ÖÖRespondents
Mr. Dharmendra Barthwal, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
Mr. Anirudh Bhatt, Standing Counsel alongwith Mr. Bhupesh Kandpal, Brief
Holder for the State.
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J. (Oral)
 By means of this petition, petitioner has sought
following reliefs:
ì(i) Issue a writ, order in the nature of certiorari quashing
the ex-parte sealing order dated 03.06.2015 passed by the
respondent no.7 herein ; quashing ex-parte and unilateral report
dated 11.06.2016 of respondent no.7 herein; quashing Office
memorandum dated 2-7-2015 whereby Additional Chief
Secretary, Industrial Development Department has withdrawn
consent/permission of petitionerís stone crusher to run the
Crusher and further quashing the Office memo dated 4-7-2015
issued by Additional Chief Secretary, Industrial Development
Department, whereby he has amended 8th line of the
cancellation of consent/permission.
(ii) To direct the respondent no.5 to consider the
petitionerís application for renewal of the petitionerís consent to
operate the Stone Crusher forthwith or within such time as this
Honíble Court deems fit in the facts and circumstances of the
present case.î
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the records.
2. Petitioner is a proprietorship firm which was
granted license for establishing a Stone Crusher at Village
Chopadia, Patti Maletha Tehsil Devprayag District Tehri
Garhwal by the Additional Chief Secretary, Government of
Uttarakhand vide order dated 04.12.2013.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that
some motivated complaints were made against the petitioner
that he is violating the conditions of license for running Stone
Crusher. He further submits that a PIL No. 63 of 2015 was

2
filed by Shri Jagdamba Prasad Rautri before this Court in
which a Division Bench had issued direction to the State
Government to look into the matter. Ultimately, Additional
Chief Secretary convened a meeting on 20.05.2015, in which
one of the partners of the Stone Crusher was also present. In
the said meeting, a decision was taken to hold spot inspection
through Divisional Commissioner, Garhwal to ascertain
veracity of the allegations made against the petitioner.
4. Perusal of the said report indicates that petitioner
had established the Stone Crusher in violation of norms fixed
by the Government and he had also breached conditions of
license for running Stone Crusher. Based on the said
inspection report, the Additional Chief Secretary has
cancelled the license granted to the petitioner vide order
dated 02.07.2015, which is under challenge in the writ
petition. The principal contention of learned counsel for the
petitioner is that petitioner was not heard while cancelling his
license, therefore the impugned order of cancellation is
unsustainable in the eyes of law.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner relied upon a
judgment dated 30.07.2015 rendered in Writ Petition No.
1884 of 2015 and submits that the controversy involved in
the present writ petition is squarely covered by the said
judgment.
6. Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate appearing for newly
impleaded respondent Mr. Jagdamba Prasad Raturi in the
writ petition submits that policy under which license was
earlier granted to the petitioner has been superseded by a
new policy. He also submits that in the writ petition, no
averments have been made against the inspection report of
Divisional Commissioner to the effect that the findings
recorded in the said inspection report are erroneous.

3
7. To this, learned counsel for the petitioner submits
that petitioner has deposited huge amount for getting license
and has also incurred other expenses in obtaining necessary
formalities for establishing the Stone Crusher. He further
submits that cause of action still survives and further renewal
of the license will also depend on the outcome of the writ
petition.
8. Since, petitioner was not heard at any stage while
cancelling the license granted to establish Stone Crusher,
therefore the impugned order dated 02.07.2015 is liable to be
quashed and is hereby quashed. The Competent Authority is
directed to pass fresh order in respect of petitioner, in
accordance with law, but only after giving sufficient
opportunity of hearing to all interested persons before taking
any decision.
9. With above observations and direction, writ petition
stands disposed of.
10. Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of
accordingly.
